html:
Roman empress from 193 to 211 as the wife of Septimius Severus, and a major power at court after him. She was born around 160 at Emesa, today's Homs in Syria, into an Arab family of priests of the sun god Elagabal.

She married Severus in 187 and bore two sons, Caracalla and Geta. When Severus became emperor she travelled with him and the army and was honoured on coins and inscriptions. She gathered writers and thinkers around her, among them Philostratus, who wrote a life of the wonder worker Apollonius of Tyana at her request.

After Severus died in 211 Caracalla had Geta murdered, by one account in her arms. She still handled much of the empire's paperwork while Caracalla campaigned. When he was killed in 217 she died soon after at Antioch, perhaps by starving herself. Her sister Julia Maesa then brought her grandsons Elagabalus and Severus Alexander to the throne, so the Severan dynasty ran through her family.
